questions.title: Gaussian kernel density estimation and AMISE
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Emanuel Parzen, On Estimation of a Probability Density Function and Mode, The Annals of Mathematical Statistics 33(3) (1962), 1065-1076, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177704472. For iid real observations X_1,...,X_n with density f, define the Gaussian-kernel estimator f_hat_h(x)=(nh)^{-1} sum_i phi((x-X_i)/h), where h>0 and phi is the standard-normal density. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation under explicit interior smoothness and integrability assumptions. Establish nonnegativity and unit integral, write the expectation as a convolution, derive the second-order pointwise bias h^2 f''(x)/2+o(h^2), derive the leading pointwise variance f(x)R(phi)/(nh)+o((nh)^{-1}) with R(phi)=1/(2 sqrt(pi)), and integrate these terms to obtain AMISE(h)=h^4 R(f'')/4+R(phi)/(nh). Minimize this expression and specialize it to a N(mu,sigma^2) density, including the normal-reference bandwidth (4/3)^{1/5} sigma n^{-1/5}. Keep finite-sample identities, leading asymptotic equalities, and rejected derivations visibly distinct; do not present AMISE, the normal-reference bandwidth, or Monte Carlo behavior as an exact theorem for arbitrary densities, boundary points, fixed h, or nonsmooth f. The required model-authored artifact is est_gaussian_kde and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public contract. Exploratory Python or R may check Gaussian integrals, equivariances, and finite-sample behavior. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment uses smooth normal DGPs, the declared normal-reference bandwidth, and predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty to compare mean integrated squared error with its exact finite-sample Gaussian expectation and its cross-n decrease. Source-code replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

source.title: On Estimation of a Probability Density Function and Mode
source.author: Emanuel Parzen

request_fields.name: sample
request_fields.meaning: The observed iid real sample used to construct one Gaussian kernel density estimate.
request_fields.shape: one-dimensional array of n>=2 finite JSON numbers; repeated observations are allowed
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, non-arrays, and lengths below two.

request_fields.name: points
request_fields.meaning: The real query locations at which the fitted density is evaluated.
request_fields.shape: nonempty one-dimensional array of finite JSON numbers; order and repetitions are preserved
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, non-arrays, and empty arrays.

request_fields.name: bandwidth
request_fields.meaning: The strictly positive Gaussian kernel bandwidth h used without data-dependent modification.
request_fields.shape: one positive finite scalar JSON number
request_fields.units: the same measurement units as sample and points
request_fields.indexing: one bandwidth for every query point
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, zero, negative values, infinities, NaN, and requests whose required density values cannot be represented as finite JSON numbers.

response_fields.name: n
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly the length of the admitted sample.

response_fields.name: bandwidth
response_fields.meaning: The bandwidth actually used by the estimator.
response_fields.units: the same measurement units as the request
response_fields.edge_cases: Must equal the admitted request bandwidth exactly up to ordinary floating-point representation.
response_fields.normalization: No optimization, clipping, or rescaling is applied.

response_fields.name: densities
response_fields.meaning: The Gaussian kernel density estimate evaluated at every requested point in order.
response_fields.shape: one-dimensional array with exactly len(points) nonnegative finite entries
response_fields.edge_cases: Repeated points produce repeated values; extreme finite points may underflow to zero, while a request whose density would overflow finite JSON representation is rejected.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly sample, points, and bandwidth; the response contains exactly n, bandwidth, and densities; implicit boolean or string coercion is forbidden.
Permuting sample order leaves every response field unchanged.
Permuting or repeating query points applies the same permutation or repetition to densities without changing n or bandwidth.
Adding the same finite constant to all sample and query values leaves density values unchanged.
Negating every sample and query value leaves density values unchanged.
Multiplying sample, query points, and bandwidth by a positive finite factor a divides every density value by a.

empirical_claims.meaning: Across each frozen normal DGP and sample size, the Monte Carlo mean integrated squared error at h=(4/3)^{1/5} sigma n^{-1/5} is compatible with the exact finite-sample Gaussian expectation under the predeclared Monte Carlo standard-error rule, and the larger-n setting has lower expected and observed MISE.

Every confirmatory replicate uses the frozen sample size, normal location and scale, normal-reference bandwidth, query grid, estimator identity, seed, and integration convention fixed before outcomes.
